P2: `mockTranscodedData.set(header, 0)` can throw when the header is larger than the allocated buffer. Guard the write or cap the header to the buffer length to avoid a runtime RangeError on small inputs.
Prompt for AI agents ```text Check if this issue is valid — if so, understand the root cause and fix it. Guard the write or cap the header to the buffer length to avoid a runtime RangeError on small inputs. @@ -0,0 +1,249 @@ + const header = new TextEncoder().encode( + `TRANSCODED_AUDIO:codec=${codec},bitrate=${bitrate},sampleRate=${sampleRate},channels=${channels}\n` + ); + mockTranscodedData.set(header, 0); + + return mockTranscodedData; ```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap initial video byte copy to destination buffer length**

The mock transcoder allocates `Math.floor(videoData.length * 0.7)` bytes, then unconditionally copies up to 100 source bytes into it. For small but valid videos (e.g., inputs under ~143 bytes), `Uint8Array#set` throws a `RangeError` because the source slice is larger than the destination, so `process()` fails instead of returning a transcoded artifact. Please bound the copied byte count (and header write) by the destination capacity.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cap initial audio byte copy to destination buffer length**

The audio mock transcoder sizes its output by bitrate-derived compression, then copies up to 100 bytes from the input without checking destination size. With default settings this throws for many short inputs (roughly any file under ~250 bytes), causing supported audio files to return an error path. Limiting copied bytes (and header length) to the allocated buffer avoids this deterministic failure mode.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Division by zero vulnerability when `videoData.length` is 0. This will produce `NaN` for `compressionRatio` which will be stored in artifact metadata. ```typescript compressionRatio: videoData.length === 0 ? 0 : transcodedData.length / videoData.length, ``` Add a guard to handle empty video data. ```suggestion compressionRatio: videoData.length === 0 ? 0 : transcodedData.length / videoData.length, ``` *Spotted by [Graphite](https://app.graphite.com/diamond/?org=21nCo&ref=ai-review-comment)*



Is this helpful? React 👍 or 👎 to let us know.

**Duplicate type declarations instead of importing from `types.ts`** `AudioTranscodeOptions` and `AudioConfig` are declared locally here and again in `src/types.ts` with identical definitions. The same duplication exists in: - `filefn/processing/src/processors/video.ts` — `VideoTranscodeOptions`, `VideoPosterOptions`, `VideoConfig` - `filefn/processing/src/processors/image-transform.ts` — `ImageTransformOperation`, `ResizeOptions`, `CropOptions`, `RotateOptions`, `ImageTransformConfig` - `filefn/processing/src/processors/ocr.ts` — `OCRConfig` Other processors (`compression.ts`, `pdf-preview.ts`, `thumbnail.ts`) already import their config types correctly from `../types.js`. These four processors should do the same: ```typescript import type { Processor, ProcessorInput, ProcessorResult, AudioTranscodeOptions, AudioConfig } from '../types.js'; ``` Having parallel type declarations means a change to `types.ts` won't be reflected inside the processor file (and vice versa), causing silent type drift. The public API exported from `index.ts` will then describe a different shape than the type the processor internally validates against.
Prompt To Fix With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: filefn/processing/src/processors/audio.ts Line: 172-183 Comment: **Duplicate type declarations instead of importing from `types.ts`** `AudioTranscodeOptions` and `AudioConfig` are declared locally here and again in `src/types.ts` with identical definitions. The same duplication exists in: - `filefn/processing/src/processors/video.ts` — `VideoTranscodeOptions`, `VideoPosterOptions`, `VideoConfig` - `filefn/processing/src/processors/image-transform.ts` — `ImageTransformOperation`, `ResizeOptions`, `CropOptions`, `RotateOptions`, `ImageTransformConfig` - `filefn/processing/src/processors/ocr.ts` — `OCRConfig` Other processors (`compression.ts`, `pdf-preview.ts`, `thumbnail.ts`) already import their config types correctly from `../types.js`. These four processors should do the same: ```typescript import type { Processor, ProcessorInput, ProcessorResult, AudioTranscodeOptions, AudioConfig } from '../types.js'; ``` Having parallel type declarations means a change to `types.ts` won't be reflected inside the processor file (and vice versa), causing silent type drift. The public API exported from `index.ts` will then describe a different shape than the type the processor internally validates against. How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Guarded assertion can let compression-level regressions pass silently.**

The `if` block on Line 407 makes this test pass even when one/both runs emit no artifacts. Assert artifact presence first, then compare sizes.


<details>
<summary>Proposed assertion tightening</summary>

```diff
-      if (lowResult.artifacts.length > 0 && highResult.artifacts.length > 0) {
-        expect(highResult.artifacts[0].data.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(lowResult.artifacts[0].data.length);
-      }
+      expect(lowResult.artifacts).toHaveLength(1);
+      expect(highResult.artifacts).toHaveLength(1);
+      expect(highResult.artifacts[0].data.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(lowResult.artifacts[0].data.length);
```
</details>
